title: Build plan groups from priority order so drain follows plan order
summary: Plan::build_with makes groups that can put a lower-priority item in an earlier group than a higher-priority one, so drain, which works groups in sequence, dispatches out of plan order. Rebuild groups from the final order: taking items in plan order, each joins the earliest group after all its dependencies' groups where it is path-disjoint with the members. Audience: operators who run `athena plan` and `athena drain` and expect them to agree.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for both behaviors; fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test required.
Fix group construction rather than reordering in batches_for.
Criteria check the dispatch order and group/order agreement.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs (Plan::build_with wave loop at ~L704-742 picks ready items of the best effective priority, then greedily groups by disjoint(); build_capped re-runs build_with on demoted copies; build_improving reorders `order` and regroups at ~L928-943) and crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (batches_for at ~L2916 only filters plan.groups in group order; drain_concurrent/run_serial work batch by batch). The entry point is the plan build used by Drain::prepare and `athena plan`. No record or data file is added, so no records validation allow-list or AnyRecord round-trip is affected. The property is measured directly: the order in which drain dispatches items, via the existing drain test harness, with max_concurrency 1.

Root cause is in group construction, not in batches_for: groups must be derived from plan.order so flattening groups equals the order. The new rule: each item, in plan order, joins the earliest group that is after the groups of all its dependencies and where it is disjoint() with all members; otherwise it starts a new group. A group must never be placed before a group holding an earlier-ordered item that it cannot join, so flattened groups == order.

Existing group tests in plan.rs (e.g. disjoint_independent_items_share_a_group_and_dependents_come_after, the ~L1747 test expecting [[b,a,c],[d]]) may need updating if the new grouping changes their expected output; update them only where the new rule justifies it.
The improvement-turn regrouping in build_improving is kept consistent with the new rule; it is not redesigned.
This change does not newly refuse any reading, so no refusal-rate criterion applies.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test (in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs tests, via `cargo test`) plans a normal item and an urgent item with disjoint touched paths and no dependency, and shows drain with max_concurrency 1 dispatches the urgent item first.

A new test in plan.rs (`cargo test -p athena-core`) shows a dependency's group comes before its dependent's group whatever their priorities, including a normal-priority dependency of an urgent item and a case where the dependent has a higher priority than its dependency.

A new plan.rs test shows that for a mixed plan the flattened Plan::groups equals Plan::order, and no later group holds an item of higher priority than an earlier group unless a dependency explains it.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.

crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs builds groups from the ordered items (earliest group after all dependencies, plan order), and its doc comments describing groups and drain order match the new behavior; crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs docs are updated where they describe group order.
CHANGELOG.md has a new entry describing that drain now dispatches in plan order when groups are involved (git diff shows the added lines).

out_of_scope: Changing priority, tier-cap, or effective-priority rules
Changing how the Steward improvement-turn promotion works
Changing the parallel scheduling or landing check logic beyond group construction
departures: Hard change touching plan grouping with existing tests that may need adjustment; slightly lower pass probability and higher cost than the reference.
hard_reason: This changes the run pipeline: how the plan orders and groups work, and therefore what the drain dispatches first.
